correlates.name: Infantile Idiopathic Scoliosis and Early-Onset Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: possibly supine and slight side-lying positioning, letting gravity cause plastic deformation of the immature thorax (Slide 15).
correlates.treatment: ideal treatment is prevention by lying infants prone - the opposite of the back-to-sleep recommendation - otherwise well-fitting orthoses and casting early in skeletal growth.

correlates.name: Juvenile Idiopathic Scoliosis
correlates.presentation: onset 4 to 10 years; more progressive than adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (Slide 17).
correlates.treatment: progression of 5 to 7 degrees indicates bracing; non-operative success is variable.

correlates.name: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS)
correlates.pathophysiology: hereditary predisposition, multifactorial; association with hypokyphosis (a thoracic spine flattened or lordotic where kyphosis is expected), a possible CNS defect, increased calmodulin (Slide 18).

correlates.name: Congenital Scoliosis
correlates.presentation: second most common category; 75 percent are progressive.
correlates.pathophysiology: vertebral malformation present at birth - hemivertebrae, wedge vertebrae, failure of segmentation (unilateral bar, bilateral fusion), fused ribs (Slide 20).

correlates.name: Neuromuscular and Acquired Scoliosis
correlates.presentation: ask whether the curve disappears with forward flexion or lying down. If it does, the curve comes from below - a leg length discrepancy - rather than from the spine; if not, consider primary postural scoliosis.
correlates.pathophysiology: the two most common neuromuscular causes are leg length discrepancy and neurofibromatosis (Slide 22).

correlates.name: Crankshaft Phenomenon
correlates.presentation: progressive severe alignment deformity, rotational and in the sagittal plane, after an apparently successful fusion.
correlates.pathophysiology: after posterior spinal fusion in a child with growth remaining, the posterior column is tethered while the anterior spine keeps growing, twisting the spine around the fusion mass (Slides 17, 80).
correlates.treatment: combined anterior and posterior fusion, removing anterior growth potential.

omm.name: Scoliosis
omm.definition: Lateral curvature of the spine in the coronal plane, usually with rotation, measuring 10 degrees or more by the Cobb method — below 10 degrees it is spinal asymmetry with no long-term significance
omm.findings: Named for the side of the convexity; the apical vertebra is the most deviated and rotated and defines the curve location; rotation drives the convex-side ribs posteriorly into a rib hump
omm.treatment: Decided by two numbers only — the Cobb angle and the growth remaining

omm.name: Structural vs Functional Curve
omm.definition: A structural curve does not resolve with rotation, side bending or forward bending; a functional curve does
omm.findings: On the Adams forward bend test a functional curve improves with side bending while a structural curve does not; a curve that disappears on forward flexion or lying down points to a cause below the spine
omm.treatment: Functional curves convert to structural through soft tissue shortening, bony change, disc degeneration and fascial fibrosis — which is the argument for treating early

omm.name: Adams Forward Bend Test
omm.definition: The screening maneuver in which the patient bends forward so the examiner can see rib asymmetry
omm.findings: Reveals the rib hump produced by vertebral rotation
omm.treatment: Screen around age 10, before the pubertal growth spurt, since children and adolescents with scoliosis are otherwise asymptomatic

omm.name: Scoliometer
omm.definition: Essentially a carpenter's level, used to measure the angle of trunk rotation on a forward-bent patient
omm.findings: Run cephalad to caudad; with a right rib hump the right side lifts and the ball deviates left. Inter-rater error is 2 degrees thoracic and 2.2 lumbar
omm.treatment: Refer at ATR 7 degrees or more, or 5 degrees or more if BMI is at or above the 85th percentile — and always state which method you used

omm.name: Cobb Method
omm.definition: A line along the superior border of the highest vertebra inclined toward the concavity and another along the inferior border of the lowest such vertebra; the curve is the angle where their perpendiculars intersect
omm.findings: Filmed standing, full length C7 to iliac crest, PA rather than AP to spare breast and thyroid — never supine, which removes gravity and underestimates the curve
omm.treatment: Place a block under the shorter leg before the film if there is a leg length discrepancy

omm.name: Risser Sign
omm.definition: A grading of iliac apophyseal ossification running anterolateral to posteromedial, from grade 0 (none) to grade 5 (full bony fusion)
omm.findings: Grade 1 appears only after peak height velocity; a lower grade means more growth remaining and greater risk of progression
omm.treatment: Bracing works only while growth remains, which is why Risser 0-2 (or Sanders 1-3) is part of every treatment decision

omm.name: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis
omm.definition: The commonest form — idiopathic curves account for 70-90% of all scoliosis — with hereditary contribution, hypokyphosis, raised calmodulin and linkage to chromosomes 17 and 19
omm.findings: Progression risk is highest in girls who are premenarchal, Risser 0, with double, thoracic, or already severe curves
omm.treatment: Observation at 11-19 degrees, bracing from 25 degrees while growth remains, surgery at 50 degrees or more

formulas.name: Scoliosis Severity by Cobb Angle
formulas.equation: Mild 10-15 deg, moderate 20-45 deg, moderately severe 45-50 deg, severe over 50 deg
formulas.meaning: Severity is defined purely by the Cobb angle, and above 50 degrees the curve begins to affect systemic function
formulas.normalValue: Respiratory function suffers in thoracic curves over 50 degrees, cardiovascular function over 75 degrees

formulas.name: Scoliosis Management Thresholds
formulas.equation: 11-19 deg observe; 20-24 deg follow closely; 25-39 deg brace; 40-49 deg brace and consider surgery above 45; 50 deg or more operate
formulas.meaning: Bracing prevents progression rather than correcting the curve, and only works while growth remains (Risser 0-2, Sanders 1-3)
formulas.normalValue: A curve of 50 degrees or more at maturity worsens about 1 degree per year for life

formulas.name: ATR to Cobb Correlation
formulas.equation: An angle of trunk rotation of 7 degrees corresponds roughly to a 20-degree Cobb angle
formulas.meaning: The two scales are not interchangeable and carry different risks of progression, so the referral note must say which was measured
formulas.normalValue: Refer at ATR 7 degrees, or ATR 5 degrees when BMI is at or above the 85th percentile
